title: Intervención pedagógica y política: desafíos del hacer investigativo crítico Pedagogical and political intervention: challenges of critical research
abstract: This paper presents a training and research experience carried out in 2024 by the Chair of Educational Research in the Education Sciences program at the National University of Salta (Argentina). In a challenging national context for public education and knowledge production, the proposal was conceived as a pedagogical and political intervention that championed the critical and transformative role of educational research. The central theme was artificial intelligence in higher education, addressing the representations, uses, assessments, and perceptions of its implications by students from all years of the Education Sciences program. Using a sociocritical approach and qualitative methodology, a collective research proposal was designed that allowed students to experience the research process, consolidate themselves as knowledge producers, and develop critical and epistemic capacities. In this context, the importance of supporting proposals that defend a public, democratic university committed to social transformation is emphasized.

title: Ampliar la trama afectiva: ESI, pandemia y cuidados. Desplazamientos frente a la emocionalización educativa Expanding the affective framework: ESI, pandemic and care. Displacements in front of educational emotionalization
abstract: This article examines the transformations of the Comprehensive Sex Education (CSE) public policy in Argentina during the pandemic, with a particular focus on its redefinition driven by the intensification of its link to the notion of care. The objective is to analyze how this consideration impacted the configuration of CSE, its effects on the place assigned to sexuality, and whether it led to desexualization or loss of specificity. The methodology includes documentary analysis, interviews with agents from jurisdictional programs, and a review of regulations and educational materials. The results show that the pandemic redefined CSE towards an emotional and relational care approach, sidelining specific aspects of sexuality and gender. This generated tensions between the universalization of the public policy and the focus on complex situations, as well as overlaps with other educational programs. It is concluded that, while this reconfiguration responded to contextual needs, it implied a certain desexualization and loss of specificity, which risks its transformative potential as a rights-based policy.

title: Editorial
Impacto de taller de educación sexual integral en población adulta LGBT+ en San Felipe (Chile) Impact of comprehensive sexual education workshop on LGBT+ adult population in San Felipe (Chile)
abstract: The study characterized the impact of a Comprehensive Sexuality Education (ESI) workshop on LGBTIQNB+ adults in San Felipe (Chile), through the development of a focus group with eight participants, to later apply the methodology of content analysis. Participants reported having received formal sexuality education prior to the workshop throughout their lives, mostly biologicist, reinforcing gender binarism and associating sexuality and sex with shame and guilt. They also received sex education informally with peers, the internet, and through pornography. In contrast, the workshop offered a broad view of sexuality: it introduced new concepts about gender, orientations and diversity, emphasized sexual health from risk reduction, consent and pleasure, contributed to professional development and strengthened community building. It is concluded that comprehensive sexuality education for the LGBTIQNB+ adult population contributed to various areas of personal development, as a form of reparation and justice for a historically marginalized population.

title: El derecho al aborto como contenido de la ESI The right to abortion as a content of CSE
abstract: We address the pedagogical presence of abortion as a subject of Comprehensive Sex Education (CSE), especially in light of Law 27610 on the Voluntary Termination of Pregnancy, (VTP) since 2021. Using a triangular approach, we propose to explore this same object of study using complementary sources. We first highlight the real conditions under which abortion is expressed in schools, based on the neoconservative advance that seeks to organize teachers and families against CSE. Second, we describe the possible paths for pedagogical approach on abortion, based on the review of curricular materials for secondary school, a quantitative analysis of the results of the 2022 Aprender test, which asked about the topicalization of abortion in schools, and interviews with secondary school teachers. Third, we highlight the necessary debates that activists have raised for the expansion of the right to VTP in conjunction with the right to CSE.

title: Potencias y desafíos de la ESI en la formación docente en Letras en dos universidades públicas en Argentina Potentials and challenges of the CSE in Teacher Training in Language Arts at two public universities in Argentina
abstract: In light of the rise of the far right and the attacks on Comprehensive Sexual Education (CSE) and sexual and gender policies in our country, we believe it is important to present a summary of the results of the 'XXX' project, which was approved in the XXX funding round. The project was approved by the XXX, through the XXX, together with the XXX, in the XXX 2022 call. We will present the results of a survey conducted among students at UNC and UNLP universities, where we work as trainers, as part of the project. In particular, we will focus on how CSE is incorporated into the explicit curriculum in relation to trainee teachers' expectations. We are therefore interested in analysing the results of the survey to facilitate dialogue between teacher training and the disciplines, and to contribute to teacher training in public universities.

title: Hijos de madres solas Children of Women
abstract: This paper offers a reflection on how early childhood education policies in the Autonomous City of Buenos Aires have — or have not — recognized children aged 0 to 3 as rights-bearing subjects. Drawing from a broader research project, the study examines how, historically, state decisions regarding early childhood have prioritized mothers’ needs over a full recognition of children’s rights, overlooking the notion of shared caregiving responsibility. Primary and secondary sources were analyzed to reconstruct the political, socioeconomic, and ideological context, as well as local and federal education policies. Legal documents, legislative debates, institutional reports, and historical records from organizations such as the Casa de Niños Expósitos and the Eva Perón Foundation were examined. The findings reveal that for a long time, children in this age group were not considered rights holders and were understood solely in relation to their mothers’ needs and aspirations, which still has effects on certain current practices and conceptions.

title: Desarrollo de la Educación a Distancia en las Universidades Nacionales de Argentina: avances y desafíos Development of Distance Education in Argentina's National Universities: Progress and Challenges
abstract: In a context where the virtualization of university education is gaining ground over traditional in-person learning, this study aims to analyze the evolution of enrollment in Distance Education (DE) programs at national universities in Argentina during the 2018-2022 period in relation to the growth in in-person programs. The research is based on two main axes: the distribution of enrollment at national universities in general and those in Greater Buenos Aires in particular. Based on a quantitative study at the national level, the data confirm the persistent hegemony of the in-person modality, although this predominance is not static, since the distance learning modality has grown more than the in-person modality during the period considered. The analysis of the situation at universities in Greater Buenos Aires reveals particular dynamics that illustrate the democratizing potential of DE in contexts of high population density and infrastructural limitations. The Argentine university system demonstrates a process of diversification in course modalities that is valuable to interpret within the framework of a historical trajectory of expansion and progressive legitimization of distance

title: La casa y los muros disciplinares: Una experiencia curricular desde la ESI The house and the disciplinary walls: a curricular experience from ESI
abstract: In this article we present some lines of reflection in relation to our own experience as members of a team in charge of the curricular construction process for secondary education teaching careers. In particular, in the task of writing the ESI curricular unit and the development of the gender perspective as a transversal training line in all fields of knowledge and curricular units. It is important to point out that, particularly, the definition of the ESI as a curricular unit was a pending subject and a demand of various sectors committed to its strengthening and consolidation as a public policy for the expansion of rights. The objective is to review the tensions, denials and appropriations caused by our sex-gendered viewpoint, materializing in discussions about the word, both in orality and in curricular writing. In this way, we propose a journey that goes from imagining the prescription of a curricular unit called ESI, to discussing how the gender perspective was transversalized in the curricular boxes of the training fields (General Training, Specific Training and Teaching Practice), to close by recovering the voices of the professors themselves who competed in these spaces and

title: La participación política en la escuela desde la perspectiva cognoscitiva de los estudiantes Political Participation in Schools from the Cognitive Perspective of Students.
abstract: The article aims to present some theoretical and methodological issues in studying political participation in schools from the students' perspective. It offers reflections that are necessary for a research project seeking to identify the cognitive construction carried out by subjects as they engage in school practices. First, it provides a state of the art review of research on the political participation of children and youth within the social sciences. Second, it reflects on students' political participation in schools, examining its diversity and its relationship with the institutional context and practices. Third, it proposes some epistemic and methodological conditions for a research program in developmental psychology, from a renewed constructivist perspective.

title: ESI y universidades. Potencias y obstáculos en el profesorado de Ciencias ambientales en Agronomía Comprehensive Sexual Education and Universities: Potentials and Challenges in the Environmental Sciences Teacher Training Program at the Faculty of Agronomy
abstract: This article presents an ongoing research project on the incorporation of Comprehensive Sexual Education (CSE) into the Environmental Sciences Teacher Training Program. The general objective of this study is to explore the intersections between CSE and Comprehensive Environmental Education in university-level teacher education. To this end, we aim to support a curriculum proposal with a gender perspective and to reconstruct the views of the participants regarding their expectations and knowledge about this intersection. The participatory action research involved interviews, class observations, and workshop records. Among the main findings, we identify the challenges surrounding the introduction of CSE in the Faculty of Agronomy, with its conservative tradition emerging as the primary obstacle. The Teacher Training and Bachelor’s programs in Environmental Sciences represent a rupture in this hegemony due to their social orientation and critical perspective on environmental conflicts. As for the potentialities, we observe an openness to gender and sexuality perspectives, which is reflected in the voices of both faculty and students. Furthermore, we argue that the inclusion of CSE has

title: Educación sexual y pornografía: Normativas y debates para situar la alfabetización pornográfica en Argentina y Chile Sex Education and Pornography: Regulations and Debates to Situate Porn Literacy in Argentina and Chile
abstract: This article analyzes the emergence of pornography as a subject of political, regulatory, and pedagogical debate within the framework of sex education in Argentina and Chile. Using a comparative approach, it examines the legal and juridical frameworks that regulate pornography in the context of recent international debates on its circulation and access. The article discusses the origins and dominant trends in porn literacy as a critical and pedagogical tool for addressing this phenomenon from an educational perspective. Finally, it reflects on the role of pornography in contemporary disputes over comprehensive sex education in both Chile and Argentina, offering key insights and possibilities for a situated approach to pornography from a critical and expanded vision of sex education.

title: El derecho humano a la educación sexual integral: Bases constitucionales y convencionales The Human Right to Comprehensive Sex Education: Constitutional and Conventional Bases
abstract: This article examines the implications of defining comprehensive sex education as a human right, based on the constitutional and treaty standards in force in Argentina. To this end, a discourse analysis is carried out on the empirical material under consideration (jurisprudence, constitutional and treaty provisions, legislation, decrees and resolutions) in order to reconstruct the scope of comprehensive sex education as a human right. Then, existing arguments from the human rights approach are distinguished. In this sense, both conceptual definitions of group incidence rights and international standards on the subject are taken into account, in particular the Inter-American system for the protection of human rights and —within it— the action of the Inter-American Court of Human Rights, to elucidate the effects of international law on local law. Conclusions. Comprehensive sex education has given rise both to a State policy and to one of the most innovative reforms in Argentine education. It constitutes a human right that is based on a strong constitutional, conventional and legislative framework.

title: Seminario Internacional de Investigación en Educación .

Violencia de género y educación sexual integral. Activismos estudiantiles en un contexto de politización feminista Gender-Based Violence and Integral Sexual Education: Student Activism in a Context of Feminist Politicization
abstract: Integral Sexual Education (ISE) in Argentina is a key public policy in the field of sexual and gender rights, although its implementation has been uneven across provincial jurisdictions as well as within educational institutions. The enactment of Law 26.150 in 2006 and subsequent advances in curricular definitions reignited a series of debates around sexuality, gender and education. This article aims to analyze the meanings that ISE has acquired among young students involved in feminist or gender-related activism, within a context of feminist politicization. Based on interviews conducted between 2018 and 2023 in various cities across Argentina, the study explores the experiences, demands, and meanings constructed around ISE, particularly in relation to gender-based violence. The research documents how youth collectives appropriate and reinterpret ISE content through feminist frameworks, while also facing tensions and resistance regarding the inclusion of gender agenda. Finally, the article raises questions about the role of schools in supporting youth through a perspective that acknowledges the diversity and complexity of sexual experiences.

title: Presentación. Dossier: Educación sexual y justicia de género. Avances, obstáculos y desafíos en la actualidad. Parte II.

title: Percepciones estudiantiles sobre los dispositivos de formación ciudadana en la escuela secundaria Student Perceptions of Citizenship Education Devices in Secondary School Percepções dos estudantes sobre os dispositivos de formação cidadã no ensino médio
abstract: This article is organized into five sections. The first section, as an introduction, frames the discussion that underpins the analysis of student perceptions in the case study of a school in Buenos Aires: the existence of two civic education devices, each with different rationalities. The second section reviews the main discussions on the construction of youth citizenship, while the third presents the methodological framework of the fieldwork. The fourth section presents the main findings regarding: (i) the content and dynamics within the civic education curricular spaces; (ii) the integration of the political context into the educational paths for the subject; (iii) the experiences and perceptions regarding student participation opportunities; and (iv) the processes of coexistence. Finally, the conclusion offers a series of reflections on the interconnections and tensions between the civic education devices in secondary schools.

title: Demandas estudiantiles sobre educación sexual en la enseñanza media uruguaya Student Claims Regarding Sex Education in Uruguayan Secondary Schools
abstract: This article problematizes comprehensive sex education from the perspective of adolescents that participate in student organizations within Uruguay's secondary education system. Drawing on digital ethnographies and analytical techniques applied to over a thousand social media posts, ten interviews, and six participant observations, the study examines the thirty active student organizations operating between 2022 and 2024. Although the notion of “comprehensive sex education” is not explicitly invoked in the discourse of these groups, their repertoires of action reveal the centrality of sexuality and gender issues in their agendas. The article analyzes six concrete initiatives in this regard: “Diversity Weeks” aimed at deconstructing dress codes, the celebration of “Pride Day,” self-organized “Sexuality Workshops,” the creation of “Women’s collectives,” protests “Against sexist Violence” during the “#8M” mobilizations, and the “Red Project” on menstrual hygiene. These student organizations' actions show strong connections with the broader Uruguayan social movement, as adolescents adopt and re-signify traditional slogans and practices from their own student and generational standpoint

title: ¿Desde dónde ver la formación de profesores? Un abordaje múltiple para contribuir al desarrollo educativo
El lugar del afecto en la enseñanza de la filosofía en educación media uruguaya “The Role of Affection in the Teaching of Philosophy in Uruguayan Secondary Education
abstract: The article analyzes the teaching of philosophy in Uruguayan secondary education within the context of the educational reform launched in 2021, which is centered on a competency-based approach. It explores the pedagogical orientations of both modern pedagogy and competency-based pedagogies, questioning what it means to “think for oneself” within each framework. Based on this analysis, it proposes a dialogue between these pedagogical orientations and the possibilities for teaching philosophy. In contrast to these dominant pedagogical approaches, the article puts forward a conception of the philosophy classroom as a collective, embodied, and affective space. To support this view, it draws primarily on the work of philosophers Marina Garcés and Sara Ahmed, who emphasize the central role of affect in critical experience. The article argues that the classroom can become a micropolitical space of resistance, capable of disrupting the forms of subjectivation imposed by the educational system and enabling new, shared, critical, and transformative ways of being.

title: En tiempos de cólera y políticas “retardadas”, la ESI avanza. Aportes para una ESI contracapacitista In times of anger and "backward" policies, ESI is moving forward. Contributions to an anti-ableist ESI.
abstract: They main objective of our qualitative research was to describe teaching and learning experiences of Comprehensive Sexuality Education (CSE) in special schools in Río Negro, Argentina. In this article we share some results regarding the singularities that CSE adopts in special schools. We also recover pedagogical experiences that deeply challenge us and invite us to redefine entrenched conceptions regarding the sexuality of people with disabilities. We analyze their vulnerable situation in the current political context, which not only devalues CSE as a public educational policy but also discriminates against people with disabilities through the use of humiliating terms in regulations, actions, and discourse. We add the possibility of thinking about how the notion of rights is manipulated from an individualistic and meritocratic perspective that fosters stigmatizing attitudes towards certain social groups. We propose resisting the advance of prevailing cruelty with a loving pedagogy that approaches an anti ableist CSE. In times of “backward" policies, we propose going for more CSE.

title: Reseña: Maestras y maestros en América Latina 1800-1950

Las políticas educativas a través del caleidoscopio: dinámicas de acompañamiento a las trayectorias estudiantiles en la educación secundaria Educational policies through the kaleidoscope: dynamics of support for student trajectories in secondary education
abstract: The implementation of policies in institutions involves creative, interactive and unstable processes that are resignified in relation to the particularities of the context and the subjects. Hence, in the view that we propose here, this set of practices conforms to a kaleidoscopic vision, in the sense of the multiplicity of subjects, dynamics and textures that are configured in the processes of interpretation and translation. Secondary schools develop different strategies that allow students to be accompanied, taking into account the inclusive meaning of the system and the mandatory nature of the level. To do this, reinterpretations are articulated, in this case of the academic regime, with the role of the teacher - tutor, which allows a view focused on the difficulties of the students. We present here some results of a qualitative design research that recovers the perspective of the subjects of the schools and how they develop devices that are institutionally designed to sharpen the gaze, put the focus on the lives of the students and personalize proposals that not only involve the pedagogical, but are installed in a more comprehensive sense of containment and training.

title: De caídas y lastimaduras: análisis etnopoético de narrativas de experiencia personal en niños argentinos hispanohablantes Of Falls and Injuries: An Ethnopoetic Analysis of Narratives of Personal Experience in Spanish-Speaking Argentine Children’
abstract: This study analyzes children’s narrative discourse of personal experience in Spanish-speaking Argentine children aged 3 to 5 years, considering its structural and rhetorical characteristics from an ethnopoetic approach and stanza analysis. Oral narratives of 120 children in different socioeconomic circumstances, obtained through individual semi-structured interviews in their educational institutions, were analyzed. The narratives were transcribed and segmented into terminal units, and then into verses, stanzas and episodes. The results reveal the presence of three narrative patterns: cyclical (49.2%), canonical (30.8%) and associative (20%), with a predominance of evaluative (46.7%) and descriptive (37.5%) information over chronological (15.8%). Children aged 5 years produce the three patterns in similar measures, while younger children show a predominance of the cyclical pattern. Children in vulnerabilized contexts tend to produce cyclical and descriptive narratives, while those in non-vulnerabilized circumstances produce more canonical and evaluative narratives. This paper highlights the particularities of the narratives of Spanish-speaking Argentine children, underscoring the ne

title: La curricularización de la ESI en la formación docente inicial: devenires y reanudamientos The curricular of ESI in initial teacher training: becomings and resumption
abstract: This article describes the process of curricularizing ESI in initial teacher training in the province of Chubut, particularly in higher education institutions, as a result of a pedagogical policy framework that created conditions for such a transformation. It also describes how its incorporation enabled modifications in the pedagogical-didactic and ethical-political approach to training, presenting scope, challenges, and new approaches within the framework of national and jurisdictional anti-rights policies. At this point, we must refer that it is prepared by recovering some results of the fieldwork carried out for the Master's degree in Education at the National University of Quilmes (2022), in the final thesis that investigated the pedagogical challenges linked to ESI in the professional development of beginning teachers of Special Education with a focus on intellectual disabilities, in Esquel (Chubut), between the years 2019 and 2022, based on the enactment of ESI Law No. 26,150 and the national and jurisdictional pedagogical political framework that began in 2006, taking as a case study graduates from the only institute with such an offer in the town.

title: Educación Sexual en Uruguay (2020-2024) Sexual Education in Uruguay (2020–2024)
abstract: This article analyzes the positions of technical-teaching staff within Uruguay’s formal education system regarding Sexual Education (SE) during 2020-2024. Contrary to national history, it was the first time the Sexual Education Program remained in force under a government that was not its original promoter. To explore how SE is incorporated in this context and analyze technical-teaching positions, the article uses a qualitative methodology based on documentary analysis of the records from the Technical-Teaching Assemblies of three subsystems. Historical tradition shows that during the so-called progressive era, SE became established in the symbolic and discursive fields, although it faced social, political, and pedagogical resistances from various sectors. The rise of conservative governments during this period, along with the implementation of regressive and privatizing policies, dealt a severe blow to the systematization of SE. It is concluded that this can be understood as a cleavage that reveals both a greater capacity for institutional re-signification centered on teachers’ appropriation of SE and a challenge and tension regarding its continuity.

title: Aproximaciones a la construcción de sentidos sobre masculinidades y feminidades de estudiantes de nivel secundario en escuelas de la ciudad de Bahía Blanca Approaches to How Secondary School Students in Bahía Blanca Construct Meanings of Masculinities and Femininities Aproximações à construção de sentidos sobre masculinidades e feminilidades entre estudantes do ensino médio em escolas da cidade de Bahía Blanca
abstract: This article analyzes the processes through which secondary school students construct meanings around masculinities and femininities. The study is developed from a qualitative and interpretative approach and was conducted in three schools with different types of administration (technical, pre-university, and confessional) through focus groups with students. Findings show that, while traditional representations persist, there are noticeable shifts toward more plural, flexible, and inclusive conceptions. It is concluded that schools function as spaces of tension between the reproduction of heteronormative norms and the possibility of transforming them. Within this framework, young people deploy various strategies of appropriation, resistance, and resignification of gender meanings.

title: Cuerpos en juego, cuerpos que disputan: discapacidad y Educación Sexual Integral. Un estudio en el departamento Paraná de la provincia de Entre Ríos. Bodies at play, bodies in disputed: Disability and Integral Sexual Education. A research in the Parana department, in Entre Rios province
abstract: This article shares insights that support the thesis entitled “Disability and Integral Sexual Education: A research in the Paraná department, Entre Ríos Province”. The research aims to collect and document the narratives of adolescents and young people with intellectual disabilities, in order to analyze their experiences with Integral Sexual Education (ESI) in Entre Ríos, Argentina. The study follows a biographical-narrative methodology and seeks to highlight the situated experiences of students. In this contribution, we present both theoretical and normative frameworks that guide the research, as well as some preliminary findings from our empirical work. We emphasize the contributions of Crip Theory -as both an analytical and political lens- understanding that it supports the problematization of the narrated experiences, dismantling the fiction of compulsory ability and challenging imposed meanings on bodies. We also recognize that ESI enables and legitimizes alternative spaces, times to disrupt ableist, cishesteronotmative structures and meanings. We advocate for a ESI that allows us to reclaim and contest our bodies at play.

title: Editorial
Infancias Trans en Argentina Trans Childhoods in Argentina.
abstract: The consideration of a gender perspective is necessary to think about trans childhoods and their educational trajectories. Gender enables certain ways of being and being in the world. The article recovers the memories and experiences about the childhoods of two adult trans people and a mother who accompanies her son's transition. A case study was carried out and semi-structured interviews were used as a data collection instrument. The results are shared from three categories: Trans childhoods from the perspective of trans adults; the educational trajectories of trans childhoods and the support for trans childhoods. Among the limitations of the study is the difficulty in generalizing the results and the need to expand the number of trans people and family members consulted.

title: Consensos, tensiones y contradicciones en la articulación entre cuerpo, salud y género en las clases de Educación Física Consensus, Tensions, and Contradictions in the Articulation of Body, Health, and Gender in Physical Education Classes
abstract: This article seeks to explore the interrelation between "healthy bodies" and the social construction of the sexed body as it materializes in Physical Education classes, based on an analysis of observations and interviews. The objective is to examine the connections that teachers establish between "Physical Education" and "health," under the premise that any inquiry into this research object would be reductionist without an analysis of the role played by the sex-gender system. To this end, a unit of analysis was implemented, composed of Physical Education teachers at the secondary level of a privately managed educational institution in the City of Buenos Aires. The findings reveal that sport emerges as the most efficient means for developing the body and promoting healthy practices. However, both the sports practices themselves and the physical qualities derived from them, as well as teachers’ expectations, representations, and assessment methods, vary according to the students' genitality. The boundaries of "healthy bodies" lie at the edge of the social construction of the "sexed body," shaped by the cultural mandate of what a body "can" or "must" be or do.

title: Neoliberalismo y educación en la era digital: tendencias y desafíos. El discurso neoliberal sobre TIC en educación: herramientas y desafíos para su análisis crítico
Reseña Elsa Freire y Paulo Freire: por una pedagogía de la convivencia de Nima Spigolon (2022) Review Elsa Freire and Paulo Freire: for a pedagogy of coexistence by Nima Spigolon (2022)
abstract: Elsa Freire e Paulo Freire: por uma pedagogia da convivência , by Nima Spigolon (2022), is part of the “Elsa Freire Triptych”1, in which the author seeks to demonstrate the true importance and the possibility of inaugurating a feminine political-pedagogical canon in the work of Paulo Freire, based on Elsa Freire’s presence in his productions. Spigolon’s book arises from the research she began in her master’s thesis and continued in her doctoral thesis at the University of Campinhas. In this first part of the triptych, Spigolon will portray the family, love, and professional life of Elsa Costa Freire from the late 1940s until 1964, when she went into exile with her family.

title: Democratización y escuelas secundarias de la Educación Permanente de Jóvenes y Adultos: un panorama desde las producciones académicas recientes Democratization and Secondary Schools in Permanent Education for Youth and Adults: An Overview of Recent Academic Productions
abstract: This article reviews recent academic productions on secondary schools within the Permanent Education for Youth and Adults (EPJA, by its Spanish acronym) in Argentina. The central hypothesis is that these institutions foster pedagogical developments aimed at educational democratization, as identified in specialized literature. Methodologically, the study is based on documentary research, analyzing federal-level productions published since 2006. The article offers an interpretative overview structured around four thematic axes: (i) public responsibility in EPJA, the quantitative expansion of educational rights, and regulatory frameworks; (ii) curricular content for youth and adults, the social function of the modality, and students’ engagement with school knowledge; (iii) representations of learners, dynamics of recognition, and subjective transformations within EPJA; and (iv) youth identities and intergenerational relationships. Drawing on the reviewed academic literature and acknowledging the complexities and underlying tensions, this work examines pedagogical conceptions, educational practices, and student experiences that contribute to greater equity within the modality.

title: ESI y re-subjetivación docente: Un estudio interpretativo en el Colegio Nacional Arturo U. Illia de Mar del Plata ESI and teacher re-subjectification: An interpretive study at the Arturo U. Illia National School in Mar del Plata
abstract: This paper shares the resonances of a research focused on the dis/re-learning that teachers undertake to develop pedagogical experiences that include sexuality in a comprehensive manner. A group of teachers from the Arturo U. Illia National School of Mar del Plata, who have been carrying out an Institutional Project of Integral Sexual Education (ESI) since 2020, participated in the study. Based on the assumption that education is always sexual, and therefore biographical and subjective, we set out to reconstruct the genealogy of the project; document the pedagogical experiences developed; analyze the contents and practices challenged by the ESI; and interpret the ways in which these experiences affect the processes of reconfiguration of subjectivities and the pedagogical perspectives of the teachers involved. From a qualitative framework and a narrative biographical approach, we mapped the daily and pedagogical experiences of the experience, analyzed documents, conducted participant observations and interviews with the teachers, the former director and the current director. Finally, we composed an inter-biographical narrative. We venture to affirm that the native category “ESI peda

title: Repensar la ESI desde el enfoque de masculinidades: una oportunidad en tiempos neoconservadores Rethinking CSE from a Masculinity Perspective: An Opportunity in Neoconservative Times
abstract: This article aims to provide an overview of the historical process of constructing Comprehensive Sexual Education (CSE) in Argentina and the need to incorporate a masculinities perspective. This approach aims to problematize the hegemonic model of masculinity that reaffirms male domination, as promoted by neoconservative sectors. In other words, it enables the possibility of conceptualizing and embodying masculinities in alternative ways. The analysis is situated within the national context of antifeminist backlash and the reaffirmation of neoconservative discourses and practices by various right-wing actors, which reinforce the perceived need to restore a masculinity eroded by the advancement of feminist policies. The article is structured as follows: first, it presents a brief historical overview and assessment of the transformations in the legal framework, educational proposals, pedagogical perspectives, and implementation strategies of this right during the early years of CSE, marked by disputes with neoconservative sectors. Second, it characterizes the dissemination and reach of neoconservative discourses and the antifeminist backlash up to the present. Finally, it examines th

title: Ofensiva conservadora en la ALESC Conservative offensive in the legislative assembly of sc (brasil): education and gender (2011-2023) Ofensiva conservadora en la Asamblea Legislativa de SC (Brasil): educación y género (2011–2023)
abstract: This article analyzes the legislative actions of right-wing and far-right parliamentarians in the Legislative Assembly of the State of Santa Catarina (ALESC), located in southern Brazil, between 2011 and 2023, focusing on proposals aimed at censorship, moral control, and the delegitimization of gender, sexuality, and diversity policies within the educational sphere. The qualitative study is based on the analysis of 67 legislative initiatives presented during the 17th, 18th, and 19th legislatures. The proposals were organized into thematic axes that reveal the centrality of education in contemporary political-ideological disputes: censorship of pedagogical and cultural materials; surveillance and criminalization of teaching practices; moralistic defense of childhood; and the imposition of conservative linguistic and cultural norms. The results underscore a coordinated and sustained offensive by the far right in Santa Catarina’s educational field, marked by legislative and symbolic actions operating through moral panics, indirect censorship, and the delegitimization of diversity policies. The article demonstrates that these actions are not merely reactive but constitute a coherent so

title: Referentes escolares de ESI: sentidos y prácticas en escuelas secundarias de Tandil (Buenos Aires) Institutional Sex Education Referents: Meanings and Practices in Secondary Schools of Tandil (Buenos Aires)
abstract: In Argentina, law 26.150, enacted in 2006, created the Programa Nacional de Educación Sexual Integral to guarantee students’ right to receive sex education at all levels of schooling, in both public and private institutions. To strengthen its implementation, the Consejo Federal de Educación issued Resolución 340/18, which promotes the formation of interdisciplinary teams of ‘referentes’ serving as referents for the “Educación Sexual Integral” program. In the Provincia de Buenos Aires, the Law 14.744 and the creation of the Dirección de Educación Sexual Integral (DESI) reinforced this framework by establishing ESI referents s at regional, district, and school levels—key figures for implementing and coordinating the educational policy. This article analyzes experiences and challenges related to the implementation of the institutional liaison role, considering the legal and regulatory framework behind its emergence, as well as its application in secondary education in schools in the Provincia de Buenos Aires. title: La negación del derecho a la información y el control de los cuerpos a través de la educación: el caso brasileño The denial of the right to information and the control of bodies through education: the brazilian case
abstract: This study analyzes how the denial of the right to information in the educational sphere acts as a form of biopolitical violence directed at feminized and sexually dissident bodies in Brazil. The objective is to understand how discourses and policies against sexual and gender education operate to restrict rights and reinforce conservative norms. Methodologically, a documentary and critical discourse analysis was conducted on legislative projects, educational regulations, and materials disseminated by political and religious actors opposing the so-called “gender ideology,” between 2014 and 2022. The results reveal a systematic offensive to exclude content related to gender and sexualities from basic education, legitimized by a moralizing discourse that frames these topics as threats to childhood and family. It is concluded that this denial of the right to information is not merely an educational omission, but a deliberate strategy of social control that especially impacts women, youth, and LGBTQIA+ individuals. title: Derechos Humanos, educación y diversidad sexual en México: los discursos y las estrategias conservadoras de la Unión Nacional de Padres de Familia Human rights, education, and sexual diversity in Mexico: the conservative discourses and strategies of the National Union of Parents of Families
abstract: In Mexico, recent governments have made progress in formally recognizing human rights and diversity —including sexual diversity— in the content of free textbooks. However, the implementation of a legislative framework and a set of educational reforms have been a source of dispute with conservative and reactionary civil society organizations such as the National Union of Parents of Families. In this context, the objective of this study is to comprehensively reconstruct the anti-rights stance deployed by the UNPF in the context of the implementation of the human rights paradigm in the field of education in Mexico. To this end, a human rights approach and a method of political discourse analysis in education are employed. The central argument is that this organization has played a key role, with veto power, in defining the educational agenda, especially regarding the content of free textbooks, adopting a political, legal, and ethical discourse to maintain its conservative thinking.
